newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power market quiet due to holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power market quiet due to holiday.

text.p: The spot market for power in the western U.S. was quiet Tuesday ahead of the Christmas holiday after prices fell sharply on Monday.
Utilities and other market players had pre-scheduled deliveries for Tuesday through Thursday because of the holiday.
Prices were pushed lower by mild weather, low holiday demand, the absence of disruptions to thermal generation and ample supplies of hydroelectric power.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Tuesday through Thursday traded as low as $16.00-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $19.00-21.00 early on Monday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Tuesday-Thursday was also sharply lower at $9.00-11.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was pegged at $15.00-$18.00, compared with $26.00-28.00 on Friday.
Off-peak Mid-C was talked as low as $9.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Tuesday-Thursday was quoted $14.00-18.00, compared with $21.00-22.00 early on Monday.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Tuesday-Thursday was quoted near $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
Next-day firm, peak prices at Four Corners were in line with PV at around $15.00-17.00 . Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was assessed at $12.00-13.00.
Cash prices for January were assessed $1.00 to $2.00 per megawatt lower than on Monday.
